questions.prompt: According to global workspace theory, a mental content becomes conscious when it...

options.text: is broadcast widely, so that many specialized processes in the brain can use it
reaches a high enough value of integrated information ($\Phi$)
becomes the target of a suitable higher-order representation
options.why_wrong: That is the condition proposed by higher-order theories.

options.text: is processed in primary sensory cortex alone
options.why_wrong: Workspace theories link consciousness to global availability, not to local sensory processing.

questions.explanation: Global workspace theory holds that many unconscious specialist processes compete, and the winning content is broadcast through a global workspace. According to the theory, that global availability is what makes it conscious.

sources.citation: Baars, B. J. (1988). A Cognitive Theory of Consciousness. Cambridge University Press.
Dehaene, S., & Naccache, L. (2001). Towards a cognitive neuroscience of consciousness: basic evidence and a workspace framework. Cognition, 79(1-2), 1-37.

questions.prompt: Who first proposed global workspace theory, often illustrated with the image of a spotlight on a theatre stage?
questions.explanation: Baars set out the theory in 1988 and later popularized the theatre metaphor: the spotlight of attention picks out what is broadcast to the audience of unconscious processes.

sources.citation: Baars, B. J. (1988). A Cognitive Theory of Consciousness. Cambridge University Press.
Baars, B. J. (1997). In the Theater of Consciousness: The Workspace of the Mind. Oxford University Press.

questions.prompt: Which pairing of theory and core claim is correct?

options.text: Global workspace theory: consciousness is the global availability of information
Integrated information theory: a state is conscious when a higher-order thought represents it
options.why_wrong: Higher-order representation is the claim of higher-order theories.

options.text: Higher-order theories: consciousness is identical to integrated information
options.why_wrong: Integrated information ($\Phi$) is the central notion of IIT.

options.text: Global workspace theory: consciousness requires integrated information above a threshold
options.why_wrong: Workspace theories appeal to broadcast, not to $\Phi$.

questions.explanation: The three theories locate consciousness differently: global availability (workspace), integrated information (IIT), or being represented by a higher-order state (higher-order theories).

sources.citation: Dehaene, S., & Naccache, L. (2001). Towards a cognitive neuroscience of consciousness: basic evidence and a workspace framework. Cognition, 79(1-2), 1-37.
Tononi, G. (2004). An information integration theory of consciousness. BMC Neuroscience, 5, 42.
Brown, R., Lau, H., & LeDoux, J. E. (2019). Understanding the higher-order approach to consciousness. Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 23(9), 754-768.
